newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Court orders Bangladesh opposition leaders release.
newsitem.headline: Court orders Bangladesh opposition leaders release.

text.p: Bangladesh's High Court on Monday ordered the release of four leaders of the main opposition Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) detained last month without charges, court officials said.
The four were arrested on March 20 and sent to jail under the country's Special Powers Act, which allows for the detention of anyone for up to four months without being charged.

But the detention can be overturned by the High Court on merit. Officials sources at the time said the four were suspected of "inciting acts of sabotage" to destabilise the government of Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina.
Court officials said the High Court had ruled that the arrest of former ministers Khandaker Mosharraf Hossain, Abdul Mannan and Goyeswar Roy, and a former mayor of Dhaka, Mirza Abbas, was illegal.
The High Court also asked the government to pay each the detainees 100,000 taka ($2,300) each in compensation.
